content:
Put the list on Readme or Homepage.

1. Understand the big picture quickly

Knowing the key papers, the main repo, and related competitions helps you grasp:

  • What CSLib actually is
  • Its goals (formalizing algorithms, data structures, concurrency, PL theory, verified software, etc.)
  • Who’s behind it and where it’s going

Without this list, you’d have to dig through arXiv, GitHub, and announcements yourself.

2. Practical reasons depending on who you are

Your Role Why the list helps you
Student / Learner Find formalizations of undergrad CS topics (algorithms with proofs, complexity, automata, etc.) to learn rigorously.
Researcher Cite the main papers, see what’s already formalized, avoid reinventing wheels, or build on existing work.
Contributor Know where to start (papers explain the vision, GitHub has the code, competitions give focused tasks).
Developer / Engineer Understand how CSLib can be used for real verified software and security-critical systems.
AI / Formal Methods enthusiast CSLib is positioned as great training data for AI theorem proving in CS topics.

3. Opportunities

  • Competitions (like the ICML 2026 challenge) are great for:

    • Building your portfolio
    • Learning Lean + formal methods
    • Networking with the community

  • Papers show you the motivation and roadmap so you can decide if you want to get involved early (projects like this grow fast once momentum builds).
